polydipsia, polyuria, & weight loss + hyperglycemia & ketonemia (or ketonuria)
Child appears acutely ill & suffers from moderate to profound dehydration
: normal glucose until 2-8am when it rises; results from ↓ insulin sensitivity & a nightly surge of counter-regulatory hormones during nighttime fasting
: bedtime injection of NPH to blunt morning hyperglycemia; avoid carbs late at night
: nocturnal hypoglycemia followed by rebound hyperglycemia d/t surge in growth hormone
: ↓ nighttime NPH dose or give bedtime snack
: a progressive rise in glucose from bed to morning
: change of insulin dose to bedtime
Random plasma glucose ≥200mg/dL + classic s/sxs of hyperglycemia
, but serum K is normal/elevated (K shift from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid)
: long-acting insulin injections 1-2x/d + rapid or short-acting insulin before each meal/snack
: delivers continuous SC infusion of rapid or short-acting insulin + supplemented boluses before each meal/snack
SIPS – saline, insulin (regular), potassium repletion, search for underlying cause
isotonic 0.9% (normal saline) until hypotension & orthostasis resolves
once serum glucose reaches ~200-250, add dextrose
*if serum glucose doesn’t fall by at least 50-70mg/dL in the first hour, DOUBLE rate of insulin infusion
regardless of serum K, pts have a large total body K deficit
give IV KCl 20-40mEq/L until K above 3.3mEq/L
check serum K q2h & delay KCl admin until serum K <5.3mEq/L
ONLY GIVEN TO PTS W/ pH <6.90
